title: Japanese expansion: Manchuria and the League (1931–1937)
summary: Why Japan's army seized Manchuria in 1931, how the League of Nations responded, and how militarists gained control of Japanese politics before full war with China.

keyterms.definition: 18 September 1931: Kwantung Army officers blew up a stretch of the South Manchuria Railway near Mukden, blamed Chinese troops and used it as a pretext to occupy Manchuria.
The Japanese army stationed in the Kwantung Leased Territory and along the South Manchuria Railway; its officers acted without Tokyo's approval in 1931.
Puppet state created by Japan in Manchuria in 1932, with the last Qing emperor, Puyi, as its nominal head.
League of Nations commission report (1932) that judged Japan's actions not to be self-defence and refused to recognise Manchukuo.
Extreme nationalism stressing loyalty to the emperor, Japanese racial destiny and expansion; spread by secret societies and young army officers.
1932 attack by young naval officers in which Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi was assassinated; it ended party-led cabinets in Japan.
Failed 1936 coup by young army officers in Tokyo; its suppression strengthened the army leadership's influence over government.
1921–22 conference that fixed capital-ship ratios of 5:5:3 for the USA, Britain and Japan, resented by Japanese nationalists.
November 1936 agreement between Japan and Germany against the Communist International; Italy joined in 1937.
Economic self-sufficiency; Japanese leaders wanted control of Manchuria's coal, iron and farmland to reduce dependence on imports.

questions.prompt: Which economic pressure most increased support for expansion in Japan after 1929?
options: The collapse of US demand for Japanese silk in the Great Depression
A sudden oil surplus that needed new markets
The loss of Taiwan to China
Hyperinflation caused by war reparations
questions.explanation: The Depression devastated silk exports and rural incomes, making Manchuria's resources and land look like a solution to Japan's crisis.

questions.statement: The Washington Naval Conference gave Japan naval parity with Britain and the USA.
questions.explanation: The 5:5:3 ratio left Japan with less capital-ship tonnage than Britain or the USA, which nationalists saw as humiliating.

questions.text: The Mukden Incident was staged by officers of the ___ Army in September 1931.
questions.explanation: Kwantung Army officers, notably Ishiwara Kanji and Itagaki Seishirō, planned the railway explosion without government approval.

questions.prompt: What did Manchuria offer Japan that made it strategically valuable?
options: Rubber plantations and tin mines
Coal, iron ore, farmland and a buffer against the USSR
Oil fields and a warm-water naval base
A direct land route to India
questions.explanation: Manchuria had coal, iron and agricultural land, and it shielded Japan's Korean colony from the Soviet Union. It did not solve Japan's oil shortage.

questions.prompt: Match each event to its year.
questions.explanation: These dates trace the decline of civilian, party-based government and the rise of military influence.

questions.prompt: Why was the assassination of Prime Minister Inukai in 1932 significant?
options: It led to Japan joining the League of Nations
It ended the era of cabinets led by political party leaders
It caused the emperor to abdicate
It triggered the Mukden Incident
questions.explanation: After the May 15 Incident, prime ministers were chosen from the military or bureaucracy rather than party leaders until after the war.

questions.statement: The February 26 Incident of 1936 was a successful coup that put young officers in charge of the government.
questions.explanation: The coup failed and its leaders were executed, but the army high command used the crisis to increase its political leverage.

questions.text: Extreme loyalty to the emperor and belief in Japan's destiny to lead Asia is called ___.
questions.explanation: Ultranationalist societies and young officers argued that corrupt politicians and businessmen were betraying the nation.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
questions.explanation: 1915, 1921–22, 1930, 1931: Japanese grievances over naval limits built up before the army acted in Manchuria.

questions.prompt: How did the civilian government in Tokyo respond to the Kwantung Army's actions in 1931?
options: It ordered the army to withdraw and the army complied
It tried to limit the conflict but failed to control the army and accepted the result
It had planned the operation in advance
It asked the League to send troops
questions.explanation: The Wakatsuki cabinet tried to localise the incident, but the army expanded operations and the government accepted the fait accompli.

lessons.title: Manchukuo, the League and the road to 1937

questions.prompt: Who was installed as the head of Manchukuo?
options: Chiang Kai-shek
Puyi
Zhang Xueliang
Wang Jingwei
questions.explanation: Puyi, the last Qing emperor, became chief executive in 1932 and emperor in 1934, while real power lay with the Kwantung Army.

questions.text: The League sent the ___ Commission to investigate the Manchurian crisis.
questions.explanation: The Lytton Commission reported in October 1932, rejecting Japan's claim of self-defence.

questions.prompt: What did Japan do after the League Assembly adopted the Lytton Report in February 1933?
options: Withdrew from Manchuria
Announced its withdrawal from the League of Nations
Accepted economic sanctions
Signed a treaty with China returning Manchuria
questions.explanation: Japan's delegation walked out and Japan gave notice of withdrawal in March 1933, exposing the League's weakness.

questions.statement: The League of Nations imposed military sanctions on Japan over Manchuria.
questions.explanation: No sanctions were imposed. Britain and France were unwilling to act in East Asia, and the USA and USSR were not League members.

questions.prompt: Which factor best explains the League's weak response to Manchuria?
options: Japan had no seat on the Council
Its major powers were absorbed by the Depression and unwilling to risk war far from Europe
China refused to appeal to the League
The USA vetoed action in the Council
questions.explanation: Britain and France had little to gain from confronting Japan, and the USA was outside the League, so it could not have vetoed anything.

questions.prompt: Put these events in chronological order.
items: Japan announces it is leaving the League
questions.explanation: September 1931, 1932, October 1932, March 1933, November 1936.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.

pairs.right: League verdict rejecting Japan's self-defence claim

questions.explanation: The Tanggu Truce (May 1933) ended fighting south of the Great Wall but left Japan in control of Manchuria and Jehol.

questions.text: In November 1936 Japan signed the Anti-Comintern Pact with ___.
questions.explanation: Italy joined in 1937. The pact signalled Japan's drift towards the European fascist powers.

questions.prompt: What was the main Chinese Nationalist strategy towards Japan in the early 1930s?
options: Immediate all-out war against Japan
Defeat the Communists first, then resist Japan
Alliance with the USSR against Japan
Recognition of Manchukuo in exchange for loans
questions.explanation: Chiang Kai-shek's policy was 'internal pacification before external resistance' until the Xi'an Incident (December 1936) pushed him into a united front with the CCP.

questions.statement: Japan's seizure of Manchuria encouraged later aggressors by showing that the League could be defied without serious penalty.
questions.explanation: Many historians see Manchuria as the first major test the League failed, a precedent noted by Mussolini and Hitler.
